summary:
Held 1 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 5 upside misses — BRBY.L +7%, III.L +6%, RAND.AS +4%, MUV2.DE +3%, ZAL.DE +2%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (EDV.L -7%, STLAP.PA -5%, BAB.L -4%, G1A.DE -4%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: EDV.L (-6.91%) — No confirmed driver for 2026-11-13. Search found only undated or older items (CEO termination, Burkina Faso permit fears), so a gold-miner or West Africa jurisdiction-risk move is possible but unverified. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: EDV.L is a UK-listed (FTSE 100) West Africa gold miner, and no strategy includes it. A gap-down on a jurisdiction or governance headline would also be unreachable for a long-only bot.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news found. The move is likely tied to Burberry's H1 FY27 interim results, which usually land in mid-November (last year's were 13 Nov 2025, +7.9%). I could not verify this for 2026.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: BRBY.L is a UK mid-cap luxury name that no strategy includes. If it was a results-day gap, an earnings-gate or gap-size filter would also have blocked a post-open entry.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a small earnings-calendar watchlist of FTSE 100/250 consumer and luxury names to the news-reactive universe. Release the earnings gate for gaps ≥ +5% on volume ≥ 2× the 20-day average within 30 minutes of the open.

top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 financials/investment trusts such as III.L to the uk-eu momentum universe, and let the earnings-gate release names that gap up 4% or more on results day with volume above 1.5x average.

top_movers.catalyst: no obvious news catalyst — searches found no Randstad news dated 2026-11-13 (last results were Q3 in October). Likely a technical, sector or staffing-peer rebound move.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely follow-through from Munich Re's final Q3 results on Nov 12 (prelim net profit ~€1.7bn beat consensus; FY guidance raised to €6.6bn). I found no Nov 13 article confirming this.

top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap EU financials (MUV2.DE, ALV.DE, SREN.SW) to the momentum universe, and let the earnings-gate admit names making a second day of post-results gains, with a gap ≥ +3% on volume ≥ 1.5× its 20-day average.

top_movers.suggestion: Add Euronext Paris large-caps such as STLAP.PA to the uk-eu universe watchlist, and log sector-wide auto drawdowns (e.g. 3+ autos down >3% on the same day) as a signal instead of requiring a stock-specific catalyst.
